Parte 2: Cirurgia

Maxwell diz: "Ah, Cirurgia. Nada faz você se sentir tão vivo quanto estar com os cotovelos mergulhados em sangue e humores. Cirurgia, como você descobrirá, meu amigo, é mais uma arte do que uma ciência. Algo está fora do lugar? Excise-o. Algo precisa estar no lugar? Costure-o. Depois que aprender o básico, meu aluno aplicado, será hora de seguir sozinho, como um filhote que cai do ninho.

Preparando o paciente

Cirurgia coloca a habilidade do cirurgião contra a força vital do paciente. As Cirurgias devem ser difíceis, e muitas podem exigir várias tentativas consecutivas antes de serem bem-sucedidas. Tenha cuidado, porém: quanto mais tempo a Cirurgia durar, mais instável o paciente pode ficar...

Tentar uma Cirurgia exige três coisas:

Um conjunto de Surgeons’ Tools. De fio de sutura a pinças, de bandagens a serras de osso, as Surgeon’s Tools contêm todo o equipamento necessário para tentar qualquer Cirurgia.

Um personagem com Proficiency em Surgeons’ Tools. Cirurgia é uma perícia especializada e impossível de tentar sem treinamento.

Um ambiente controlado. Isso significa um local estável, livre de ameaças e distrações durante toda a Cirurgia. Idealmente, uma sala dedicada; no mínimo, um acampamento estável.

Concentração. Cirurgia exige Concentração, portanto o cirurgião não pode manter Concentração em uma Spell ao mesmo tempo em que realiza a Cirurgia.

 

Iniciando a Cirurgia

Quando os três requisitos acima forem atendidos, um personagem pode iniciar o desafio de perícia. Cada rodada do desafio ocorre da seguinte forma:

Teste de Surgeon’s Tools. O personagem que tenta a Cirurgia faz um Ability Check com Surgeon’s Tools (geralmente usando Dexterity ou Intelligence), contra a DC da Cirurgia. Cada tentativa leva 30 minutos. Se o personagem igualar ou superar a DC, a Cirurgia será bem-sucedida. Se não alcançar a DC, ainda não terá sucesso e poderá tentar novamente.

Dano aos Hit Points Máximos. O personagem submetido à Cirurgia sofre Dano em seus Hit Points máximos igual ao Hit Die de sua Class (por exemplo, um Barbarian sofre 1d12 de Dano em seus Hit Points máximos). If the DC is failed by 10 or more, the character undergoing Cirurgia takes two hit dice worth of Dano to their max Hit Points instead. This Dano represents trauma to o corpo through Cirurgia and loss of blood. It occurs whether or not the Cirurgia was a success.

Decision to Continue. If the DC was not met, it increases (cumulatively) by 1. The surgeon may choose to either proceed with Cirurgia and make another surgeons' tools ability check or abandon the Cirurgia.

Dying Patients. If the character's maximum Hit Points are ever reduced to 0, they are dying. If the surgeon imediatamente abandons the Cirurgia at this point they are stabilized and regain 1 to their max Hit Points. If the surgeon proceeds with the Cirurgia, the character dies.

 

Assisting with Cirurgia

Maxwell diz: "I always strive to have the maximum available amount of hands possible, both in my help and on my patients."

Second Surgeon. A character may use the help action to assist with Cirurgia only if they are also proficient in surgeons' tools. In this case, the surgeon rolls their surgeons' tools check with advantage.

Assessing the Patient A character proficient in Wisdom (Medicine) may assist the surgeon by assessing the patient's condition. After max hit point Dano is done, they may roll a Wisdom (Medicine) ability check:

If the surgeon chooses to assess the patient, they make their next surgeons' tools ability check with disadvantage. Splitting their attention between the patient's vital signs and the Cirurgia itself is distracting and they need their whole focus to do their best surgical work.

Other Ways to Help. Any spell, ability, or mechanic that gives advantage or a bonus to Ability Checks functions as normal, but only pertains to a single surgeons' tools check unless its duration extends beyond 30 minutos. These include bonuses gained from effects such as (but not limited to) Inspiration, Bardic Inspiration, Guidance, Enhance Ability, and the Lucky feat.

 

Recovery

Dano to maximum Hit Points inflicted by Cirurgia recovers at a rate of 1 class HD + the character's Constitution modifier per Long Rest. For example, a Barbarian with a Constitution score of 18 would recover 1d12 + 4 to their maximum Hit Points depois de um Long Rest. The Greater Restoration spell cures this Dano to maximum Hit Points as usual.

 

Finding a Surgeon

The adventuring party should be able to find surgeons in any major city with little trouble, though they may not be cheap. The average surgeon charges 500 gold for a Cirurgia, and the most skilled surgeons charge up to double that (though for a higher success rate, it may be worth the money).

Finding a surgeon in a mid-sized town or smaller village is more difficult. There is a 50% chance an NPC proficient with surgeons' tools resides in any given mid-sized town, and only a 10% chance in a smaller village. Even if the party manages to find someone who knows their way around a scalpel, often these people are more used to treating injured farm animals than they are people.

 

List of Common Surgeries

Below is a collection of standard surgeries that you are able to perform with a set of surgeons' tools. The specific Cirurgia required for each different injury is listed in the Tratamento area of the Lingering Injuries Tables.

Cirurgia Geral

Cirurgia Geral is the most standard Cirurgia and can be used for a wide variety of applications. Removing the broken tip of a weapon from inside someone, stitching back together a perforated bowel, or removing Necrótico tissue so a wound can properly heal would all be considered Cirurgia Geral. Cirurgia Geral has no additional rules or requirements unless they are listed in the Tratamento section of a lesão.

Teste de Resistência Cirurgia Sensorial

A Teste de Resistência Cirurgia Sensorial attempts to Teste de Resistência one of the character's senses, such as vision or hearing. Reconstructing a slashed ear or neutralizing Ácido splashed into an eye are examples of injuries requiring a Teste de Resistência Cirurgia Sensorial. Sensory structures are generally delicate and small, and as a result, all one is often able to do is repair the surrounding area, apply salves and bandages, and hope for the best. As a result, you may only ever make one surgeon's tool's ability check for a Teste de Resistência Cirurgia Sensorial. If it is not successful on the very first try, then the Cirurgia was a failure. After a Teste de Resistência Cirurgia Sensorial, characters must wait 1d4 dias antes de they remove the bandages and dressings to see if the Cirurgia was successful.

Teste de Resistência Cirurgia de Membro

A Teste de Resistência Cirurgia de Membro is attempted when you want to reverse Dano done to a limb or small appendage. Reattaching a severed limb, treating an immolated arm, or reconstructing a crushed leg are all examples of injuries requiring a Teste de Resistência Cirurgia de Membro. When a limb is ausente, the surgeon is racing against the clock. Each hour that the limb é considerado ausente antes de the Cirurgia begins increases the DC of the Cirurgia by 1. A Gentle Repose or Feign Death spell cast on the limb eliminates this DC increase for their duration. A limb recovering from this type of Cirurgia is weaker than normal and takes a penalty similar to if the Resurrection spell had been cast on it: O membro takes a −4 penalty to all attack rolls, Saving Throws, and Ability Checks requiring its use. Every time the character finishes um Long Rest, the penalty is reduced by 1 until it disappears.

Amputation

Sometimes a body part is beyond saving. Sometimes a character is bitten in the arm by a werewolf and wants to prevent lycanthropy by any means necessary. For those occasions, there is Amputation. Amputation grants the ausente condition to a body part. Amputation's DC is always 10. 29
